inputs.original_text: This is a power grab dressed up as security policy. The bill would make death the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis, and Ben-Gvir’s religious party is pushing it—but the real objective is to make unequal justice and extreme state power feel routine. The debate itself helps sell that shift. Even the opponents’ denunciations may just provide the appearance of resistance while the machinery keeps moving.
inputs.modified_text: This is bigger than Ben-Gvir’s party pushing a bill. The whole debate looks engineered to make unequal justice and expanded state power seem normal: supporters advance the policy, while opponents denounce it in ways that can make the process look contested and legitimate. The outrage may be part of the cover. The machinery keeps moving, and the death penalty becomes easier to sell as routine.
